the development of an approach to the measurement and analysis of educational performance.
the use of examination results as indicators of school and college performance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at present, the use of examination results for accountability purposes in the United Kingdom is inappropriate and misleading and that the government should abandon this practice.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
value‐added comparisons have the potential to be a useful research tool but are unlikely to be useful for accountability purposes.
the use of examination results as indicators of school performance is not a useful policy.
the current system is not a good one and the only way forward is to use the value‐added approach to identify institutions that need further investigation and, if necessary, intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current system for the publication of examination results in league tables is not an adequate substitute for more detailed, individual‐level analyses.
the current use of examination data for accountability is inappropriate and that a more sophisticated use is required if the data are to have any real meaning for the public.
the use of examination data as the principal basis for judging the performance of institutions is likely to be a major source of confusion, and possibly even injustice.
